top_story.headline: Immigration agency extends GEO Group's Aurora, Colorado detention contract without competition days before it expires
top_story.dek: The justification says the facility holds more than half of Colorado's detention beds and that the competitive replacement contract is still being evaluated.
paragraphs: U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement is adding a two-month sole-source option period (Oct. 16 to Dec. 15, 2026) to its contract with The GEO Group, Inc. for detention and transportation services at the Denver (Aurora) Contract Detention Facility. According to the justification (J&A-26-0417), posted Oct. 13, the current contract, 70CDCR22D00000001, expires Oct. 15, 2026. The estimated value is redacted, and the agency cites urgent need as its authority to skip competition.

The justification says the competitive follow-on acquisition “is in the evaluation phase” and that the extension will let the agency “complete the ongoing competition, make an award, and transition” to the new contract. It says the Aurora facility “currently provides capacity for up to 1,530 detainees, representing more than half of the available detention bed space in Colorado.”

One detail stands out: the extension relies on Federal Acquisition Regulation clause 52.217-8 (Option to Extend Services). The justification says the clause is in the current contract but “wasn’t evaluated at the time of award,” and that this “will be the first use of the 52.217-8 for this contract.” The same clause is how the agency says it avoids a gap in service for its Enforcement and Removal Operations office. Related immigration-custody items today include a brand-name Zscaler network order for the same agency (Sole-Source Justifications) and a plan for 250 secure beds for unaccompanied migrant children (Presolicitations).

sections.headline: Navy gives Lockheed Martin $15 million more in no-bid work on nuclear-armed cruise missile facilities, a follow-on to an uncompeted 2026 award
paragraphs: 46 new sole-source justifications today, 15 of them posted under other notice types (award notices, special notices and sources sought); 6 repeats from earlier editions were left out. The GEO Group detention extension in Denver is today's Top Story and is not repeated here. An unusually heavy day: six justifications are written up as full cards.

blocks.text: Must read

blocks.title: Air Force plans a no-bid contract for an airshow “Air Boss” at Dover Air Force Base
meta: William David Schultz (named in the notice title)
blocks.text: The Department of the Air Force's Dover contracting office posted, as a Special Notice, an intent to award a sole-source contract to “WM. David Schultz” for Air Boss and narration services at the base's June 12-13, 2027 open house. The vendor field is redacted, so the name comes from the notice title. The summary of the attached draft performance work statement lists qualifications such as years as a military airshow Air Boss, 200 warbird hours, $1 million in liability insurance and experience with the Blue Angels or Thunderbirds; the screening found no competition or market-research document attached.

blocks.title: Navy gives Lockheed Martin $15 million more in no-bid work on nuclear-armed cruise missile facilities
meta: Only one company can do it
Department of the Navy, Strategic Systems Programs
blocks.text: The Strategic Systems Programs office wants Lockheed Martin Corporation to provide facilities engineering and warhead-planning services for the Nuclear-armed Sea-Launched Cruise Missile (SLCM-N) program, including on-site engineers at the Strategic Weapons Facilities in the Atlantic and Pacific, from Oct. 1, 2026 to Sept. 30, 2027. The justification says the work “is a follow-on to the fiscal year 2026 contract award to LM, which was not competed,” and that a new contractor “would require an estimated 24 to 36 months to acquire the necessary facility clearances.” It was posted as an Award Notice, which lists a $9,629,380 award dated Sept. 30.

blocks.title: Pentagon's Washington Headquarters Services sole-sourced Marriott for a 600-person Washington conference, with the justification posted after it ended
meta: Justification value redacted; award notice lists $724,742
Department of Defense, Washington Headquarters Services
blocks.text: Washington Headquarters Services awarded lodging and catering for 600 government attendees at a conference, check-in Sept. 29 and check-out Oct. 1, 2026, in the Washington area to Marriott Hotel Services Inc. The award notice lists $724,742 dated Sept. 25; the justification was posted Oct. 13, after the event. It argues that, because of citywide bookings, recurring international summits and large conventions, no other property could house all 600 people “under one roof” for operational security and force protection. It was posted as an Award Notice and refers to an “Office of Secretary of War” conference.

blocks.title: Air Force buys $58.9 million more Tactical Airborne Communication Kits from Baxter Aerospace without competition
meta: Only one company can do it
blocks.text: The justification adds more kits, spare units and parts, test assets and field service representatives (including overseas deployments) to an existing contract, FA861226CB002, which it says was itself awarded because of “the unusual and compelling urgency of Operation Epic Fury.” After that award, it says, “the USG quickly realized other items were critical to the warfighters' use of this capability but not included in the scope of the contract.” Baxter Aerospace is described as the only proven vendor currently producing and shipping the kits. The estimated delay from competing is redacted.

blocks.title: Air Force sole-sources missile-defense command-and-control sustainment after a coverage lapse left a forward unit without its air picture
meta: Only one company can do it
blocks.text: The Air Force says it needs an undefinitized contract action to keep Air Base Air Defense System for Missile Defense command-and-control systems supported, because the original manufacturer holds the source code and the government “does not possess the technical data and license rights” for another contractor to take over. The justification describes a recent administrative lapse in contract coverage that caused a 100% loss of the command-and-control air picture for a forward-deployed Pacific Air Forces unit, and cites Executive Order 14186 (Golden Dome for America) timelines. It frames the action as a bridge while the program moves to a competitive follow-on. The vendor name and value are redacted in the posted copy.

blocks.title: Defense Contract Management Agency commits up to $90.5 million to its ServiceNow platform through Carahsoft with no competition
meta: Only one company can do it
blocks.text: The Defense Contract Management Agency plans a task order under an existing Defense Department enterprise software blanket purchase agreement held by Carahsoft Technology Corp. The total is $90,467,667.83 over a base year plus four option years, to sustain its ServiceNow platform, add 17 capabilities (including Foreign Military Sales budget tracking and general-counsel fraud detection) and buy licenses. The justification says only a source with the incumbent's “unique qualifications and deep institutional knowledge” can avoid “unacceptable delays and substantial duplication of costs.”
Also worth a look

items: National Aeronautics and Space Administration (IT Procurement Office) — annual site license and maintenance for Peraton's OS/Comet software in the Artemis launch control system; urgent need, no time to compete; value redacted; the document cites Executive Order 14369 (80TECH26P0025).

Defense Information Systems Agency, for the Navy — Innovatus would run a Pilot Integration Team moving software pilots into the Navy's Flank Speed Azure cloud; limited-source order, value redacted; the justification says only Innovatus knows the custom architecture (832675104).

Army Contracting Command, Detroit Arsenal — posted as a Special Notice, but it is a competitive Ground Maneuver Commercial Solutions Opening; amendments add counter-drone detection and mobile camouflage areas of interest, and an earlier amendment describes buying 1,000 drone-to-drone interceptors and eight ground control stations (W912CH-26-S-0001).

Department of Health and Human Services, Program Support Center — RIVA Solutions, Inc., the incumbent, for website operations and maintenance plus an AI chatbot added after market research; value unverified (7571MN26F80158).
U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement — brand-name Zscaler Inc. Zero Trust Branch hardware and implementation through Carahsoft; value redacted (JA-26-0258).

Department of Veterans Affairs, Network Contract Office 02 — two Beckman Coulter bridge awards: $1,400,180 for East Orange (36C24226Q0983) and $1,635,120 for downstate New York medical centers, where the justification says “a post-award protest was filed” on the earlier effort, “resulting in a corrective action” (36C24226Q0974).

Defense Contract Management Agency — Poplicus, Inc. d/b/a Air Enterprise, 12 AI/ML analytics licenses, $1,813,602; the justification says a sources-sought notice “yielded zero capable vendors” (S5121A26FE025).

blocks.text: Other sole-source justifications (routine parts, renewals, maintenance, small buys): Department of Homeland Security — 3 (70CDCR22D00000001_P00026, the Top Story; 70Z08426PDL930042; REQCIO-26-00-095); Department of Education — 1 (91003126Q0015); Department of the Army — 1 (JA-26-EDG-0518); Department of State — 1 (19AQMM26C0023); Department of Veterans Affairs — 7 (36C10B27Q0039, 36C26227P0047, 36C24226Q0983, 36C24727F0020, 36C77623C0089, 36C255-27-AP-0365, 36C10B27Q0038); U.S. Special Operations Command — 1 (2026_RFI_GDMST_TACLANE_Products_Justification); Securities and Exchange Commission — 1 (50310222A0008-50310224F0163); Defense Logistics Agency — 9 (SPRDL1-25-R-0065, SPE2DH24D0006SPE2D427F0062, SPE2DH24D0006SPE2D427F0061, SPRTA126F0238P00001, SPE4A7-27-C-0006, SPRRA1-24-R-0007, CL25339003, SPRPA126RYC01, SP060426C8000); Defense Health Agency — 1 (HT001426CE021); National Aeronautics and Space Administration — 2 (80TECH26QA114, 80MSFCPS500926); Library of Congress — 1 (2027-LGD-0065); Department of the Treasury — 1 (2031ZA26P00137); Department of Justice — 1 (15B11327P00000001); Department of Health and Human Services — 1 (7571MN26F80044); Department of Agriculture — 1 (127EAB16L0204).

sections.headline: Boeing gets $611.5 million without competition for the first MQ-25 Stingray production lots
paragraphs: 317 new award notices, 30 of them flagged; 78 repeats from earlier editions were left out. Border-infrastructure maintenance contracts and a rare public-interest-exception construction award at a Navy munitions center round out the day, so four items get cards.

blocks.title: Boeing gets $611.5 million without competition for the first MQ-25 Stingray production lots
meta: Department of the Navy, Naval Air Systems Command
blocks.text: The Naval Air Systems Command says it awarded a sole-source modification (N0001922C0048 P00017) to The Boeing Company on Sept. 17, 2026, covering MQ-25 Low-Rate Initial Production Lot 1 and the Lot 2 Advance Acquisition Contract. A justification attached to the notice says “awarding any of the efforts required for this contract to a source other than Boeing would result in an unacceptable delay of over 4.5 years,” and notes MQ-25 was a designated Maritime Accelerated Acquisition program. A separate Boeing sole-source plan for fiscal 2027 MQ-25A spares appears under Presolicitations.

blocks.title: Navy invokes the “public interest” exception for a $26.5 million munitions-center upgrade
meta: Department of the Navy, Naval Surface Warfare Center, Indian Head Division
blocks.text: The Naval Surface Warfare Center, Indian Head Division restricted competition under FAR 6.302-7 (public interest) with a Determination and Findings, then awarded a firm-fixed-price contract of $26,508,270 to The Whiting-Turner Contracting Company of Towson, Md., on Oct. 13 for an upgrade titled “BXXXX for Inert Preparation.” The public-interest exception is rare; the notice does not say what the determination found.

blocks.title: Koman Advantage wins $177 million in two border contracts
blocks.text: U.S. Customs and Border Protection awarded Koman Advantage, LLC a $136,580,298 contract for tactical infrastructure maintenance (dated Aug. 31, 2026, solicitation 70B01C25R00000038) and a $40,573,952 contract for Carrizo cane eradication in Texas (dated Sept. 30, solicitation 70B01C26R00000114). Both are firm-fixed-price; the posted descriptions say nothing more.

blocks.title: Border wastewater plant adds construction packages in a $552 million award notice
meta: PCL Construction Inc. dba PCL Construction Services
International Boundary and Water Commission: U.S.-Mexico
blocks.text: The International Boundary and Water Commission: U.S.-Mexico posted a modification to the South Bay International Wastewater Treatment Plant rehabilitation and expansion progressive design-build contract with PCL Construction Inc. It adds Early Work Package 1C (roof, equipment, piping and electrical replacement, $13,147,453) and Early Work Package 3B (long-lead equipment procurement, $25,693,528). The notice lists the award at $552,372,021 dated Sept. 29, 2026 and does not say how much of that is new.

items: U.S. Customs and Border Protection — El Paso and Big Bend North tactical infrastructure maintenance; TIMS 8a JV LLC, $45,839,723 (70B01C26R00000096).
Department of the Army (Aberdeen Proving Ground contracting office) — Small Arms Protective Inserts body armor for Foreign Military Sales; Hardwire LLC, $35,000,000 (W91CRB-26-R-A006_SAPI).
Department of State (U.S. Embassy Manila) — group health insurance under a master contract; PhilHealthcare, Inc., $18,729,946 (19RP3827D0001).
Defense Logistics Agency (Disposition Services) — hazardous waste removal for Eastern Europe and Israel; Sued-Muell GmbH & Co. KG, $16,460,362 (SP450027D0001).
Defense Logistics Agency (Aviation) — cable assemblies bought from Federal Prison Industries, Inc., $42,286 (SPE4A626Q0430).
Department of the Army — research award to Ludwig-Maximilians-Universitat Munchen (University of Munich) for replacing PFAS chemicals in infrared decoy flares, $1,106,487 (W912HQ27CA002).

blocks.text: Also flagged, not written up: Veterans Healthcare Supply Solutions $95,168; East Coast Medical $6.7 million ceiling; Philips North America $861,217; GE Precision Healthcare $465,168; Parking Veterans $2,196,000; Blue Cord Design and Construction $12,974,316; Bravo, Inc. $3,410,433; Golden State Medical Supply $15,270,520 (a 2024 award posted now); Architechture Solutions $2,966,021; Stone Group Architects $3,400,000; Teledyne Instruments $3,915,464; General Electric $488,268; JB Contracting $79,957; VAL-PRO $34,396,650; Datix $2,204,605; Chemring Energetic Devices $2,341,754; 1984 Levin Living Trust lease $2,154,979; Krueger International $24,097,180; Skyspares Parts $350,000. The other 287 award notices were routine, 251 of them from Defense Logistics Agency offices (Land and Maritime 129, Aviation 67, Troop Support 55). 78 repeats from earlier editions were left out.

sections.headline: Space Development Agency opens bidding on missile-warning ground stations under a $369 million contract ceiling
paragraphs: 156 new solicitations, 61 flagged; 20 repeats from earlier editions were left out, and five flagged notices already listed this week were omitted because their latest change was only an amendment or new deadline. An unusually heavy day: four cards.

blocks.title: Space Development Agency seeks bids for ground entry points for its missile-warning satellite constellation
meta: Department of the Air Force, Space Development Agency
blocks.text: The Space Development Agency's final request for proposals FA240126R0003 covers site civils, procurement, installation, integration and testing of communications shelters, antennas, optical terminals and networking equipment at “multiple, globally dispersed locations” for its Resilient Missile Warning Tracking low-Earth-orbit ground entry points. The ordering-procedures attachment says total orders “may not exceed the IDIQ ceiling amount of $369,000,000.” A cost-reporting plan spreadsheet says Kratos will flow requirements down to subcontractor Peraton, Inc., and the evaluation factors treat engineering from small and non-traditional contractors as “a strength.”

blocks.title: Navy tanker charter requires armed security teams to repel pirate and terrorist attacks and bars crews from China, Iran, North Korea and Russia
meta: Department of the Navy, Military Sealift Command
blocks.text: Military Sealift Command request for proposals N3220527R6011 (Tanker Voyage Charter) seeks a double-hull tanker able to carry at least 15,000 barrels of clean product. The attached terms require contractor security teams to stop boarding by a force of as many as 15 people and to “defend the vessel against pirates or terrorists who may use 2 to 20 small vessels simultaneously… armed with automatic weapons and rocket propelled grenades.” The security firm must hold ISO 28007 certification, officers and crew may not include citizens of “China, Iran, North Korea, or Russia,” and the Red Sea, Bab al-Mandeb Strait and Gulf of Aden are listed as imminent-danger-pay locations.

blocks.title: Defense Logistics Agency wants JP-5 jet fuel trucked from Houston into Mexico with no U.S. security escort
meta: Department of Defense, Defense Logistics Agency Energy
blocks.text: Defense Logistics Agency Energy solicitation SPE608-26-R-0206 covers fuel transportation from Houston to Progreso, Mexico for Nov. 1, 2026 through Oct. 31, 2027. The Q&A says “the movement of the product must be by road across international borders,” and the performance work statement says “the U.S. Government will not provide security escort for trucks transporting fuel product” to the Port of Progreso. A read of the solicitation, not verified word for word, puts the requirement at up to 20,000 gallons a month.

blocks.title: Interior Department seeks a caterer for a Nov. 17 reception at the National Museum of the American Indian for foreign dignitaries
blocks.text: The Department of the Interior's Office of International Affairs wants full-service catering, staffing and rental equipment for a post-program evening reception for REACH 250 (Repatriation and Exchange for American Cultural Heritage) on Tuesday, Nov. 17, 2026, at the Smithsonian National Museum of the American Indian in Washington. Quoters must cite experience with events involving “foreign dignitaries, senior government officials, or other high-level participants,” show menus with Native American-inspired culinary traditions and be an approved museum vendor; no deposit is paid.

items: Department of Homeland Security (agency not shown on the notice) — heated 24-foot double-arm inbound commercial gate at the Houlton, Maine Land Port of Entry, wired to backup power and operated from the Customs and Border Protection officer booth (47PC5226Q0134).

Department of the Army (Army Contracting Command, Rock Island) — multiple-award contract for Special Ammunition and Weapon Systems and non-NATO standard ammunition for the Defense Department, other agencies, foreign governments and international organizations; the solicitation bars sourcing from Russia's financial, energy and defense sectors (SAWS-W519TC26RA036).

Department of the Air Force (Hill Air Force Base) — SABER V construction contract limited to 8(a) firms in Utah, Nevada and Wyoming; proposals due Nov. 5, and an unverified read of a solicitation amendment lists a $490,000,000 maximum (FA820126R0020).

General Services Administration — modernize 17 elevators at the Thurgood Marshall U.S. Courthouse in New York, estimated at $30 million to $40 million, with a project labor agreement evaluated at the lesser of 10% or $15 million off the bid (47PB5126R0018).

Department of the Air Force (Life Cycle Management Center) — MJU-76/B infrared countermeasure flares, multiple-award contract with a $9,446,336 Year 1 affordability cap for 5,000 units and an estimated $200,000 qualification-testing cost borne by bidders (FA821326RB005).

Military Sealift Command — time charter of a U.S.-flag offshore supply vessel for submarine rescue support in Hampton Roads, able to handle a 419-short-ton rescue system, lay days Feb. 18 to Mar. 28, 2027 (N3220526R6077).

blocks.text: Other flagged solicitations not written up include Fort Hood aircraft refueling (two-person crews for VIP and congressional-staff flights), Navy Electronic Chart Display and Information System production, Naval Station Newport King Hall dormitory repair, Fort Rucker Aviation Maintenance II, Marine Corps East barracks industrialized construction and a Bureau of Prisons residential reentry center in Raleigh. The largest routine groups were 28 from U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Louisville District, and 4 each from Army Contracting Command Rock Island, Defense Logistics Agency Aviation at Oklahoma City and Department of Veterans Affairs offices. 20 repeats from earlier editions were left out.

sections.headline: Defense Department Education Activity solicits an esports program for 12 Pacific high schools
paragraphs: 383 new combined synopsis/solicitations, 48 flagged; 57 repeats from earlier editions were left out, and flagged notices already listed this week with only an amendment or deadline change were omitted.

blocks.title: Defense Department schools agency wants a contractor to run esports at 12 Pacific high schools
blocks.text: The Department of Defense Education Activity (titled “Department of War Education Activity” in the notice) seeks a contractor for consulting, program planning, logistics and competition and event execution for an interscholastic esports program across 12 Pacific Region high schools. The government keeps program management through a contracting officer's representative. The notice gives no value.

blocks.title: Grand Canyon North Rim needs 662,000 gallons of water hauled in by Oct. 29
meta: Department of the Interior (agency line blank in the notice)
blocks.text: Solicitation 140PP027Q0008 seeks water hauling for the North Rim; a vendor question in the Q&A records a 662,000-gallon base quantity with completion required by Oct. 29, 2026. A statement of work read by the screening pass, not verified word for word, attributes the need to an Aug. 29 flash flood that damaged the Transcanyon Waterline and left the North Rim's Roaring Springs pump house inoperable.

blocks.title: Navy plans a sole-source order to Lockheed Martin for F-35 infrared test equipment
meta: Department of the Navy, Naval Air Systems Command
blocks.text: The F-35 Lightning II Program Office, part of the Naval Air Systems Command, intends to issue an order under Basic Agreement N00019-24-G-0010 to Lockheed Martin Aeronautics Company for a test system that injects synthetic electro-optical infrared imagery into an F-35 under test. It continues work under N00019-23-F0017 and cites the only-one-responsible-source authority (10 U.S.C. 3201(a)(1)), saying Lockheed is the sole designer and developer.

items: Defense Logistics Agency (Land and Maritime) — pressure relief valve, quantity of two, delivered to USS Gerald R. Ford (CVN 78) within five days of award, approved sources only (SPE7M127T0909).

Department of the Army (Fort Liberty contracting office) — temporary shower trailers for the 1st Battalion, 505th Parachute Infantry Regiment, 82nd Airborne Division, during an off-post exercise at Camp Lejeune (W9124727QA002U00001).

Defense Logistics Agency Energy — government-owned, contractor-operated fuel services at Naval Air Weapons Station China Lake, set aside for service-disabled veteran-owned small businesses; closing date moved from Oct. 16 to Nov. 9 (SPE60326R0530).

Naval Air Warfare Center, Weapons Division — two manufacturer sole-source software notices: a JetBrains toolbox renewal (N6893627Q0006) and AdaCore GNAT Pro Enterprise support for 15 users (N6893627Q0004).
Department of the Air Force (Air Force Sustainment Center, Warner Robins) — flight data recorder and amplifier control unit for C-130, C-17 and C-5 aircraft, competed (FA853927QB002).

Department of the Air Force (Air Force Sustainment Center) — precision timeservers for the Royal Saudi Air Force and Japan Air Self-Defense Force; the sole-source justification says Boeing designed the mission computing to work only with this timeserver (FA813926Q0030).

blocks.text: Other flagged notices not written up include National Aeronautics and Space Administration brand-name TESCOM valves for Artemis launch support, Army Supply Chain Optimization Support at Fort Bliss and Redstone Arsenal, Pipeline and Hazardous Materials Safety Administration research announcement and exclusive-use helicopter services at Yosemite. The 335 other new notices were routine, 299 of them from Defense Logistics Agency offices (Land and Maritime 126, Troop Support 103, Aviation 70). 57 repeats from earlier editions were left out.

sections.headline: Government plans to contract up to 250 secure and heightened-supervision beds for unaccompanied migrant children
paragraphs: 57 new presolicitations, 18 flagged; 13 repeats from earlier editions were left out, including the Department of Veterans Affairs' $40 billion disability-exam draft request, which was already listed. The first card comes from a document read today on a notice posted earlier.

blocks.title: Government plans a single contract for up to 250 secure and heightened-supervision beds for unaccompanied children
meta: Up to 150 secure and 100 heightened-supervision beds
Administration for Children and Families, Office of Refugee Resettlement
blocks.text: This comes from attached documents read today on notice 75751MN27R00002. The performance work statement says the Office of Refugee Resettlement needs contractor-provided facilities for children in its custody, with a minimum initial capacity of 30 secure care and 30 heightened-supervision beds available within 120 calendar days of award, scalable up or down as directed. It describes secure facilities as having “a secure perimeter, major restraining construction inside the facility, and procedures typically associated with correctional facilities,” and allows restraints and seclusion only “in limited situations” of emergency safety, consistent with state law.

blocks.title: Navy plans a second no-bid Boeing deal: fiscal 2027 spares for the MQ-25A drone
meta: Department of the Navy, Naval Air Systems Command
blocks.text: The Naval Air Systems Command intends to use Basic Ordering Agreement N00019-26-G-1002 to negotiate fiscal 2027 spares and repair equipment, in phases, with The Boeing Company for the MQ-25A Stingray, citing the only-one-responsible-source authority and describing Boeing as the sole designer, developer and manufacturer. The same program's production lots are in Award Notices today.

items: National Institutes of Health — notice of intent to sole-source radiopharmaceuticals from Cardinal Health 414, LLC, not to exceed $900,000, citing “the past 25 years of contracting with this vendor” (NOI-OD-27-000001).
National Institutes of Health — sole-source dry cleaning of comforters for the Edmond J. Safra Family Lodge on the Bethesda campus to Tom's Cleaners LLC (NOI-OD-27-000182).
National Institutes of Health — two-month bridge contract for pediatric oncology support at the Clinical Center and National Cancer Institute, to Guidehouse Digital LLC (NOI-OD-27-000467).
Court Services and Offender Supervision Agency — parking for 15 vehicles within a third of a mile of 800 N Capitol Street NW, Washington, one base year plus two six-month options (9594CS27Q0001).

U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Detroit District — cutting lead service line connections at the corporation stop and removing about one foot of lead line in Detroit's public right of way (PANGLR-26-P-0000027925).

General Services Administration — 3,138-square-foot expansion for a federal law-enforcement office in Austin; the advertisement says weapons will be stored on site and “individuals may be temporarily detained and/or questioned” (4TX1001-3).

blocks.text: Other flagged presolicitations not written up include Bettendorf, Iowa flood repairs, Hawaii Air National Guard F-22 egress shop, Hi-Rel circular connectors sole-source intent, Nashville VA garage suicide prevention, Nebraska-Western Iowa VA temporary chillers, Navy SeaPort public-affairs support and USNS Lansing post-shakedown availability. The other 39 new notices were routine, led by Defense Logistics Agency Aviation at Oklahoma City (6) and Naval Supply Systems Command Weapon Systems Support (7). 13 repeats were left out.

sections.headline: Space Command's roughly $4 billion headquarters facility moves toward a design-build challenge
paragraphs: 47 new special notices, 21 flagged; 8 repeats from earlier editions were left out. Three cards: the Space Command facility, a Trident missile engineering contract and a classified sole-source.

blocks.title: Army announces design-build competition for a roughly $4 billion Space Command facility
meta: Department of the Army, Army Contracting Command, Rock Island
blocks.text: Army Contracting Command, Rock Island gave advance notice of a challenge statement for the United States Space Command Command and Control Facility. The industry announcement says the facility and its data center support “approximately 1,800 personnel and cost approximately $4B,” and will include radio-frequency shielding, high-altitude electromagnetic pulse protection and SCIF construction. The government will brief industry at the Huntsville, Alabama Industry Day on Oct. 21.

blocks.title: Navy says Lockheed Martin Space will get the next Trident II and W93 reentry engineering contract
meta: Department of the Navy, Strategic Systems Programs
blocks.text: The Strategic Systems Programs office says it will award an engineering services contract to Lockheed Martin Space for fiscal 2025-2028 production and deployed system support, W93/Mk7 aeroshell design, development and production, reentry body flight and ground tests, and Trident II D5LE2 work, which includes architectures and preliminary designs to “alter and extend the D5LE missile life.” Solicitation reference N0003024C0100.

blocks.title: Strategic Capabilities Office sole-sources to a joint venture of its two current prime contractors
meta: Department of Defense, Strategic Capabilities Office
blocks.text: The Strategic Capabilities Office says it released a notice of intent on Sept. 30 to sole-source “Mission-Critical Support Continuity” to Technical Capabilities Group, LLC, a joint venture of its two current prime contractors, identified in the notice as MTSI and SPA, to ensure uninterrupted support for transitioning advanced technologies to urgent warfighter needs. The full notice sits on a classified acquisition portal.

items: General Services Administration (Technology Transformation Services) — request for information on inherited credentials for Login.gov so users can reuse prior identity verification; the attachments cite Office of Management and Budget memo M-26-18 and call for evaluating attributes including Social Security number, date of birth and ID number plus AI-flagged behavioral biometrics (47QPCA27RFI0001).

U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Louisville District — Fort Carson Equipment Concentration Site, to be built with a construction manager at risk under Other Transaction Authority (10 U.S.C. 2808a); a formal request for qualifications was issued Oct. 13 with responses due Oct. 28 (W912QR-IndustryDay-FortCarsonECS-CMARwithOTA).

Army Contracting Command, Watervliet Arsenal — continuously open Commercial Solutions Opening for Watervliet Arsenal and Benet Laboratories through Sept. 30, 2027; areas of interest include radial forging tooling, an automated line for minor cannon components and converting the chromium plating facility (W911PT26SC001).

U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Wilmington District — virtual industry day for a “scope dredge to budget” approach to Texas ports; an unverified read of the draft scope lists $54.62 million for the Houston Ship Channel and $28.5 million for Galveston Harbor and Channel (W912PM27RA006).

Transportation Security Administration — Industry Day Oct. 20 at its Springfield, Virginia headquarters on Horizon 25 OrchestrateSI and TalentSI: integrated airport operations and talent acquisition (TSAHorizon25_OSI-TSI_FY2027).

Naval Surface Warfare Center, Crane Division — sources sought for overhaul and repair of the SPG-62 antenna and MK82 director for the MK99 fire control system, the illuminator for the Aegis weapons system; personnel need up to SECRET clearances, and seven of eight attachments are access-restricted (N0016427SNB01).

blocks.text: Other flagged special notices not written up include sole-source intents for North American Mfg Pros, Space Data Association, Doble Engineering, Benchmark Space Systems and Encore Holdings, plus National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration satellite mission operations, Winfield Locks and Dam rehabilitation, Keyport logistics support, Hanscom fire station and terminal, Joint Base Elmendorf-Richardson vehicle maintenance shop, Veterans Affairs pharmaceutical industry day and Fort Campbell aircraft hangar. The other 26 new notices were routine (National Aeronautics and Space Administration 6, Defense Logistics Agency Aviation Oklahoma City 3, others 1-2 each). 8 repeats were left out.

sections.headline: FEMA seeks executive jets with priority phone lines to the White House
paragraphs: 93 new sources-sought notices, 37 flagged; 18 repeats from earlier editions were left out. Four cards, plus two late document findings in the list.

blocks.title: FEMA seeks executive jets with priority phone lines to the White House
meta: Department of Homeland Security, Federal Emergency Management Agency
blocks.text: The Federal Emergency Management Agency wants a senior executive aircraft lease whose in-flight telephone system has “dedicated, priority-routing capabilities allowing instant, high-clarity connection to the White House, the Homeland Security Council, and others such as the FEMA National Response Coordination Center.” The performance work statement also calls for airborne LiDAR to produce disaster-damage maps and survivor coordinates via satellite links. An unverified read says it asks for two jets on dedicated call, departing from the National Capital Region, preferably Reagan National Airport.

blocks.title: Veterans Affairs asks industry for enterprise alternatives to its current productivity and security software
blocks.text: The Department of Veterans Affairs is researching enterprise solutions for productivity and collaboration, security and compliance, case management, low-code development and source-code management, and the document says a July 28, 2026 policy memo means alternatives need not hold FedRAMP certification to be considered. The screening summary reads this as a search for alternatives to Microsoft; the quoted text does not name Microsoft.

blocks.title: Federal Bureau of Investigation asks about food franchise rights in the Washington region
meta: Department of Justice, Federal Bureau of Investigation
blocks.text: The Federal Bureau of Investigation posted RFI0026 asking organizations for requirements, processes, documentation and marketing materials related to obtaining food franchise rights in the National Capital Region, with a direct-engagement model for industry feedback. It commits the government to nothing.

blocks.title: Energy Department offers to hand private firms stockpiles of critical minerals at old nuclear sites
meta: Department of Energy, Office of Environmental Management
blocks.text: The Department of Energy's expression of interest says legacy inventories at the Paducah plant in Kentucky include “approximately 8,000 tons (56 million pounds) of aluminum and 2,000 tons (4 million pounds) of copper,” that Oak Ridge holds about 12,000 pounds of lithium hydride, and that about 16.2 million tons of uranium mill tailings sit in the Moab disposal cell. Any recovery would remain subject to characterization, decontamination and regulatory approval.

items: Department of the Air Force (Air Combat Command) — sources sought for contractor-owned, contractor-operated counter-small-drone service; an unverified read lists a 95% threshold neutralization rate (FA4890-261013).

U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Fort Worth District — B-21 Field Training Detachment Facility at Dyess Air Force Base, shifted from traditional design-bid-build to an Other Transaction agreement to speed delivery (W9126G28RB210).

Department of the Air Force (Kessel Run) — AI-enabled airbase emergency-management software designed for threats such as hypersonic weapons, cruise missiles and drone swarms; Secret clearance required before award and a top-secret facility clearance before fielding (FA8730-26-RFI-C2IMERA-WARDEN).

Defense Information Systems Agency — electromagnetic spectrum IT modernization, moving legacy spectrum systems onto the Maven Smart System; contractors are barred from hands-on platform coding to avoid conflicts of interest (632675877).

Department of Homeland Security (Office of Health Security) — two requests for information: enterprise occupational medicine and medical surveillance, including pre-employment mental-health screening (70RWMD26RFIP00003), and an occupational-health electronic health record system (70RWMD26RFIP00005).
Naval Surface Warfare Center, Philadelphia Division — MTU diesel engine lifecycle support through a Basic Ordering Agreement expected with Rolls-Royce Solutions America (N64498-25-RFPREQ-PD-42-0014).

Department of Veterans Affairs (late finding from a document read today on an earlier notice) — a draft product description for document-control software for about 400,000 personnel requires bias-evaluation documentation and disclosure of third-party changes to AI model outputs, with a corrective action plan within 10 business days of any material deviation (36C10B26Q0830).

Department of the Army, Aberdeen Test Center (late finding) — the Data Collection Support Services work statement says the contractor “shall use AI platforms and tools in preparation of all documentation” (W91CRB-26-0000_043711).

blocks.text: Other flagged sources-sought notices not written up include Joint Base Lewis-McChord vehicle barrier replacement, Federal Emergency Management Agency Deployment Management Solution, Search and Rescue Satellite-Aided Tracking operations, Birmingham nurse call system, Army defense market intelligence subscriptions and Navy consolidated trailer acquisition. The other 56 new notices were routine, led by Defense Logistics Agency Aviation (6). 18 repeats were left out.

sections.headline: General Atomics drone-production modification of $56.5 million leads a Defense backlog batch
paragraphs: No new awards of $2 million or more were featured. The Defense Department's 90-day-delayed release this week brought 40 new awards of $2 million or more (all just made public after the hold), 4 large modifications and 3 cuts, two of which are featured. Everything below was signed July 14, 2026 and published this week. The 41 routine actions are listed, each linked, in “USAspending: Every Other New Award” at the end of the edition.

blocks.text: General Atomics Aeronautical Systems, Inc. — +$56,530,178, Department of the Army, modification P00029. Signed July 14 and published this week; Defense Department contract data is released with a 90-day delay. This supplemental agreement for work within scope definitizes Option 2 of the Production Readiness Test Assets effort, an unmanned aircraft contract, which means final pricing terms were set. The record gives no further detail on the aircraft. (award)

Lockheed Martin Corporation — −$46,590,606, Department of the Army, modification P00016. Signed July 14 and published this week. This supplemental agreement for work within scope reduces a contract described as the purchase of High Mobility Artillery Rocket System (HIMARS) M142 launchers for the United States and Foreign Military Sales partners. It is not flagged as a termination, and the record does not say whether work was ended, reduced or money returned. (award)

Institute of International Education Inc — −$7,739,328, Department of Defense / Defense Human Resources Activity, modification P00014. Signed July 14 and published this week. A supplemental agreement removes money from the Boren flagship grants, fellowships and scholarships contract; the record does not say why. (award)

footer.known_gaps: No source errors were reported. OMB Apportionments: no new or flagged files were found, and no changes were detected in the reviewed Spending Plan documents (manifest at 8,347 entries). SAM.gov documents: 1,951 attachments on 403 notices were identified; 102 were access-restricted on SAM.gov and 143 were queued for a later edition, and 1 file failed to read. In total 171 files are queued and will be read over the next editions, with anything they turn up reported as a late finding. 736 links to outside portals (such as DIBBS and the Procurement Integrated Enterprise Environment) were not followed. Findings marked unverified were treated as leads, not facts.
